trigger: Family gathering where mother-in-law observes the cord and insists on alcohol cleaning; FTM feels unable to override the authority figure.
context: FTM 26F; mother-in-law present in household during first weeks; hospital instruction contradicted by elder family member; FTM lacks confidence to push back.
behaviour: Posted to r/beyondthebump describing the conflict
Identified the generational advice gap explicitly
Sought community validation to override the elder's instruction
constraint: Social hierarchy — elder family member's authority carries weight even when medically wrong; FTM doesn't want to create conflict.
thought: My mother-in-law did this with her kids and they were fine. Maybe the hospital is being too cautious?
fear: Damaging the relationship with mother-in-law while trying to protect the baby.
emotional_stake: Torn between medical authority and family authority; fear of being a 'bad' daughter-in-law or a 'bad' mother.
exact_language: I should be washing his umbilical cord area and wiping it down with rubbing alcohol. I looked at her and said no. But she said but I did that with you and your sibling and you guys were fine.
